text:
sophia: quick sync — we need to prioritise the streaming semantics for chat/completions. a couple of customers (finance + search startup) pushed resumable streams + deterministic finish reasons as must-haves.

jake (eng-runtime): +1. high level tradeoffs: SSE is simpler for browser clients and proxies, WS gives bidirectional control and multiplexing. resuming over SSE is awkward unless we implement an explicit resume token flow.

maria (pm): customers care about two flows: 1) resume after transient network drops (mobile / flaky proxies), 2) clear finish reasons so downstream logic can detect truncation vs normal completion. those should be launch gates.

kevin (devex): SDK impact: we'll need client helpers for parsing deltas and normalizing finish reasons across transports. if we pick SSE default we still should support WS for advanced cases. SDKs should expose a unified event API: onDelta, onFinish({reason}), onResume.

jake (eng-runtime): proposed server model: keep a single canonical delta format (json-lines) with types: "delta", "meta", "finish". resume token included in meta every N tokens. example:```
{"type":"delta","chunk":"I like"}
{"type":"delta","chunk":" pizza"}
{"type":"meta","resume_token":"r_abc123"}
{"type":"finish","reason":"stop"}
```
This maps cleanly to SSE event lines and to WS messages.

tariq (customer-success): from customers: resume token must be deterministic across restarts of the same model version (so they can resume without model drift). also they want an explicit "truncated" finish reason when we hit token limits.

maria (pm): launch criteria suggestion:
- spec: canonical delta format + finish reason enum (stop, function_call, error, truncated, stop_sequence)
- SDK helpers in Node + Python + browser (unified events)
- telemetry: per-token latency + resume/fallback counts + finish reason breakdown
- backward compatibility: existing non-streaming endpoints remain stable
- docs + migration guide with examples for SSE and WS

kevin (devex): rollout plan: beta for dedicated customers first (they can toggle), SDKs behind feature flag, collect errors for 2 weeks, then broad launch. need a small example repo for each transport.

jake (eng-runtime): operation concerns: resume requires server-side KV of recent prefixes by resume token. we should limit retention (e.g., 2 minutes) to control memory. also need a way to validate resume token belongs to same model/version.

sophia (product): prioritization asks: is WS necessary for MVP or can we ship SSE + resume token? aim is fastest path with minimal infra changes.

jake (eng-runtime): technically we can ship SSE + resume token MVP. WS adds multiplexing and lower-latency two-way control but increases compatibility testing. if we do SSE first, design should be transport-agnostic so WS can be added later without changing delta format.

maria (pm): decision: SSE-first, canonical delta json-lines, finish reason enum including "truncated". WS as follow-up P2.

tariq (customer-success): relay to customer A that resume + truncated finish reason are in the plan; ask whether they need WS specifically and capture their feedback.

kevin (devex): action items:
- create SDK PR templates for Node/Python/browser (feature-flagged) — @kevin
- docs + spec draft by EOW — @maria
- runtime design doc for resume tokens and retention limits — @jake
- telemetry signal definitions (finish_reason, resume_success, resume_failure) — @kevin + ops-bot to create ticket

ops-bot: created ticket PROD-STREAM-17 for telemetry signals.

sophia: thanks — I'll put SSE-first + finish reasons + resume tokens into the initiative doc and mark WS as follow-up. please comment on spec doc when ready.

jake (eng-runtime): one more thought — add explicit "fallback" event so clients can detect when we served a lower-quality model variant during overload. important for routing policies.

maria (pm): noted. add "fallback" to meta events; include it in telemetry breakdown.

kevin (devex): +1. plan looks actionable. small reminder: ensure CORS and proxy behavior for SSE examples (mobile proxies can buffer lines).

sophia: great. I'll spin up the initiative ticket and link the spec. leaving this thread open for spec comments. :white_check_mark:
